title: output-wire-protocol-and-tool-binding-acceptance-criteria
creator: Ava Patel
description: Define clear, testable acceptance criteria for the output wire protocol and tool/function binding behavior. This ticket covers schema handshake, streaming partials, error classification and recovery behaviors, idempotency for tool calls, backpressure and resumability semantics, and required telemetry to validate correctness in Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Schema handshake: client->server 'schema_version' and optional 'schema_uri' are accepted; server returns an explicit acceptance envelope (status: accepted|rejected) before emitting structured frames.
Field-level typing: For any declared schema, the runtime must validate emitted fields at runtime and tag violations as VALIDATION_ERROR in the envelope with a stable error code (SO-VAL-01).

Streaming partial objects: The runtime supports emitting partial JSON objects as 'frames' (frame_type: open|field|close|checkpoint). A well-formed stream must always end with a close frame or an explicit terminal error envelope.

Checkpoint semantics: Checkpoint frames must include a monotonic checkpoint_id and a minimal provenance header (model_id, model_version, request_id). Server must guarantee client can resume from a checkpoint_id within 72 hours in Hosted and Dedicated modes.

Tool binding handshake: When function/tool calling is requested, server must emit a function_invocation_intent frame listing candidate tool bindings (tool_id, version, required_inputs). The client (or orchestrator) must confirm the binding before the tool invocation occurs.

Idempotent tool calls: All tool invocations must include an idempotency_key computed from (request_id, invocation_sequence). Retries with the same idempotency_key must be deduped by runtime or tool gateway and return the original response if available.

Partial result reconciliation: If a stream is interrupted (network or server failover), upon resume the runtime must (a) re-emit checkpoint summary frames up to last-acknowledged checkpoint and (b) mark any toggled fields as 'tentative' until revalidated by the model and schema-checker.

Backpressure handling: If the runtime detects downstream backpressure, it must emit a backpressure_notice frame and switch to aggregated batching mode within 50ms for that request path. Aggregated frames must still conform to schema envelopes.

Error taxonomy and recovery: Define recoverable vs terminal errors. Recoverable errors (THROTTLE, TEMP_BACKEND, TRANSIENT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH) allow automatic retry according to exponential backoff; terminal errors (SCHEMA_VIOLATION, PERMISSION_DENIED) abort with a terminal envelope and human-readable remediation hints.

Graceful fallback to plain-text: For clients that do not accept structured frames, runtime must gracefully degrade to a plain-text stream with an initial deprecation_notice frame containing structured-fallback-metadata. Fallback must be opt-in via client header 'Accept: application/redwood+json' absent => fallback.

Observability guarantees: For every function call and structured emission, runtime must emit correlated telemetry: trace_id, request_id, schema_version, tool_id (if invoked), checkpoint_id, frames_emitted_count, and terminal_status. Each telemetry event must be searchable in Console within 15 minutes of emission.

Compatibility window: Schema evolution must support 'additive fields' without breaking existing consumers. Any non-additive change requires 'compatibility_hint' in the handshake and a staged rollout with a canary that validates backwards-compatibility on at least one dedicated customer workload before general rollout.
Performance SLOs: Structured-streaming median first-frame latency must be <= 120ms in Hosted and <= 80ms in Dedicated under nominal load; checkpoint resume latency <= 300ms for <=512-token resumes.

Test harness: All acceptance checks must be exercisable from the maintained structured-output test harness and produce deterministic pass/fail artifacts stored under the test-run bucket with test_run_id included in telemetry.

Security: Invocation of tools that access customer data must require explicit 'allow_tool_binding=true' on the customer config profile in Private deployments and must be audited in the audit log with tool invocation arguments redacted by KMS policy.
test_plan: Unit: schema-validator unit tests for 15 representative open and closed schemas (expect pass/fail matrix).

Integration: end-to-end stream test that opens a schema handshake, emits 3 partial objects, simulates transient network drop, resumes from last checkpoint, and validates deduplicated tool_invocation outcomes.
Chaos: run fault-injection in Dedicated (network partition between front-proxy and runtime) and confirm resume semantics and telemetry completeness for 5 consecutive runs.
Compatibility: schema evolution test where consumer reads using older schema while producer adds optional fields; assert no parse failures in 1000 synthetic messages.
Load: 10k concurrent structured streams for 1 minute against a staging Dedicated cluster to validate median first-frame latency SLOs.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated release: prod flag 'structured_output_v2_wire' default off.
Canary step: enable for 3 internal teams and 1 low-traffic enterprise customer for 72 hours; collect schema-violation rate and function-invocation error delta.
Automated rollback: if schema_violation_rate > 0.5% over 15m or function_call_failure_rate increases by 20% relative to baseline, automatically disable flag and open incident runbook.
Full rollout: staged per-region over 7 days with monitoring checks after each region.
telemetry_requirements: Metric: structured_frames.emitted_count (tags: region, environment, model_id, schema_version)
Event: function_call.attempt (fields: request_id, invocation_id, idempotency_key, tool_id, status)
Trace: end-to-end.trace including handshake->frames->tool_binding->terminal_envelope with span annotations for checkpoint/resume events
Dashboard: streaming-health panel with 15m rollup showing first_frame_latency_p50/p95, checkpoint_resume_latency_p50/p95, and validation_error_rate.
